bull_bear.body:
- Process depth as the core advantage: Electron Beam Welding for high-precision shunts, Diffusion Bonding and Cold Bonding for bimetal and trimetal platforms, and precision strip processing for consistency and yield
- Develops machinery and process capabilities in-house, strengthening its ability to scale capacity with greater control
- R&D-led platform built over four decades on in-house know-how, proprietary manufacturing depth and close customer collaboration
- Long qualification discipline and specification intensity in customer applications creates stickiness; customer qualification is cited as a source of stickiness
- 300+ customers including OEM and Tier-1 across 38 countries, with exports at 56.66% of FY26 revenue
- Balanced product platform — bimetals and shunts as mature base, contacts adding switching depth, PCB/busbar assemblies as the next integration layer — giving multiple entry points into customer systems
- Pricing power and value capture: FY26 revenue grew despite a 0.6% decline in standalone volumes, on improved average realisations and a mix shift toward component sales
- Regional diversification across India, Europe and Asia reduces dependence on a single demand pool
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer and geographic concentration — The largest single exposure has historically been to a small number of marquee customers and to the US market, where a key shunt account drove much of the Americas' revenue. FY26 crystallised the risk: as that customer normalised inventory amid the North American EV slowdown, Americas shunt revenue fell about 23%. Mitigation is diversification across 38 export markets and four product lines, with India, Europe and the rest of Asia carrying more of the load, and a wider customer base through the new assemblies and contacts businesses.
- Tariff and trade risk — As an exporter earning over half its revenue abroad, the Company is exposed to the shifting tariff landscape and geopolitical disruptions to trade flows. It mitigates through geographic diversification, a local European presence in Milan for direct EU access, and a flexible Indian manufacturing base benefiting from China-plus-one reorientation; management monitors trade-policy developments and adjusts market and pricing strategies.
- Raw-material (silver / nickel / copper) price volatility and forex exposure — Production costs are sensitive to key metal prices, principally silver for contacts as well as nickel and copper, which can be volatile. With more than half of revenue in foreign currency the Company is also exposed to exchange-rate movements. Mitigation: broader supplier network, alternative sourcing, inventory buffers for critical materials, backward integration into select bimetal inputs, and forex hedging.
- New-segment execution and margin dilution in the assemblies ramp — The pivot into PCB and busbar assemblies carries execution risk — scaling a new manufacturing line, qualifying with demanding automotive OEMs and managing a learning curve. In its ramp phase the new line carries lower net margins than the mature portfolio, so a faster mix shift toward assemblies could dilute blended margins near-term. Managed by building on existing EBW capacity, phasing capacity in line with demand and prioritising margin quality and disciplined capital allocation.
- Technology obsolescence and cyber risk — Product relevance depends on staying ahead of evolving customer and industry standards, addressed through continuous R&D and market monitoring by an in-house government-approved R&D facility. As operations digitise, cyber threats such as data breaches could cause financial loss, regulatory penalties and reputational harm; the Company is strengthening its cybersecurity framework and resilience.
- Handling hazardous material and waste (BRSR material issue) — Handling hazardous material and waste in operations can directly affect the health and well-being of employees and the surrounding community. Managed through occupational health and safety standards, the EHS Policy, supplier collaboration on emerging risks, regular quantitative risk assessments with closed action plans, an Emergency Response Plan and safe plant design principles.
- Workplace safety (BRSR material issue) — Manufacturing activities involve employees operating plant systems, machinery and material-handling equipment, each of which inherently carries a risk of injury, with potential medical expenses, compensation claims, legal liabilities, regulatory penalties, operational disruption and reputational damage. Managed through compliance with safety regulations, the EHS Policy, stringent protocols and continuous training.
- Artificial intelligence governance, algorithmic bias and data ethics (BRSR material issue) — Deployment of AI/ML systems without robust oversight creates risks of algorithmic bias, automated discrimination, privacy violations, data leaks, IP infringement and non-compliance with emerging AI/data-protection regulations, with potential regulatory fines and legal costs. Planned mitigation includes an AI Ethics & Governance Framework with human-in-the-loop oversight for critical automated decisions, regular algorithmic fairness and data-privacy audits, enterprise data governance and encryption, and employee upskilling.

business.body: Shivalik Bimetal Controls Limited manufactures thermostatic bimetal and trimetal strips, low-ohmic shunt resistors, electrical contacts, busbar connectors and PCB assemblies, whose products operate inside electrical, electronics, automotive, industrial, switchgear, smart metering, battery management and energy management systems. It serves a diversified portfolio of over 300 customers including OEMs and Tier-1 automotive suppliers, smart-meter manufacturers, switchgear and electrical-equipment companies, renewable-energy and energy-storage system integrators and industrial power-electronics customers across 38 countries, with exports contributing 56.66% of FY26 revenue (BRSR states exports at 56.65% of turnover). The stated direction is to move beyond supplying critical current-carrying and protection components towards higher-value components, assemblies and integrated solutions, with bimetals and shunts as the mature technology base, electrical contacts adding switching depth and PCB and busbar assemblies forming the next layer of integration.

outlook.body:
- Build forward from the core: shunts, bimetals, contacts and assembly platforms are to work together as part of a broader precision technology architecture, making Shivalik more embedded, relevant and valuable within customer systems
- Move from strip to finished components and from components to integrated assemblies, so that value captured per customer relationship rises
- Use the Pune facility to strengthen capability in PCB and busbar assemblies for automotive and electrification-led applications, positioning the Company closer to OEM and Tier-1 customers
- Forward integration through a new manufacturing facility at Pune, Maharashtra for automotive busbars, connectors and their assemblies, focused on PCBA and busbar assembly solutions for e-mobility, energy storage and allied applications
- In Electrical Contacts, move towards more value-added contact components where quality, tooling capability and transparent pricing strengthen customer trust
- Geographic diversification: India anchoring the core, Europe as a growth engine and Asia contributing momentum, while continuing to treat North America as a strategically important long-term market
- FY27 focus on disciplined execution and capital allocation — demand-backed procurement, tighter working-capital management through accelerated cash collections, and phased capital deployment aligned with evolving customer programmes
- Keep R&D as the foundation of the next phase — adding new product platforms, deepening technical differentiation and converting precision materials expertise into higher-value solutions
- The governance sections in this bundle state no dividend, balance-sheet or reinvestment philosophy. The only capital-allocation item present is the AGM notice's ordinary business: "To confirm the payment of Interim Dividend and to declare Final Dividend on equity shares for the financial year ended March 31, 2026". Form AOC-1 records no proposed dividend from any of the three subsidiaries.
- BRSR Section B states the Company has NOT yet formalised specific ESG commitments, goals or timelines; it lists ongoing initiative areas instead — transition towards green and renewable energy, waste management, tree plantation, quality education, good health and well-being for vulnerable and marginalised groups, and zero hunger
- Transition towards green and renewable energy: electricity is sourced primarily from hydro power grids and solar panels have been installed across facilities; MD&A adds that the predominantly hydroelectric supply keeps Scope-2 emissions effectively negligible and the Company is progressively transitioning toward renewables, particularly solar
- Waste management in compliance with environmental regulations: plastics recycled through the Municipal Corporation, e-waste handled by authorised vendors, hazardous waste disposed of via Shivalik Solid Waste Management Limited, and other waste including ETP sludge treated as per applicable norms
- Tree plantation: over 600 saplings planted in and around the manufacturing facilities during FY 2025-26 in collaboration with the Forest Department, Solan (Himachal Pradesh) — the third consecutive year of the initiative, which the Company commits to continuing and expanding
- Policies covering all nine NGRBC principles are board-approved and translated into procedures, and take into account recognised national and international certifications and standards such as ISO 9001, ISO 14001 and ISO 45001
- Occupational health and safety anchored on an Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) Policy, regular safety and emergency preparedness training and an Emergency Response Plan; capability building in advanced manufacturing, quality systems and customer qualification is a stated priority as the Company moves up the value chain
- Human capital: a workforce of over 1,000 people based principally at the Himachal Pradesh campuses, with headcount and employee costs up about 25% at the consolidated level in FY26 to scale capability for the new assembly line and the Pune facility; the in-house R&D unit has been government-recognised since 2002 with R&D intensity around 1% of revenue
- Community: through a board-approved CSR policy and CSR Committee, community investment is directed toward education, health and local development around operations, including support to local government schools through infrastructure enhancement and educational development initiatives
- ESG governance: the Company reports under the BRSR framework and reviews its ESG strategy against global standards and stakeholder expectations, with oversight by board committees including Audit, Nomination and Remuneration, Stakeholder Relations, CSR and Risk Management
- Product purpose alignment: the Company frames its shunts, thermostatic bimetals, contacts and assemblies as enabling components of the energy transition — embedded in electric vehicles, smart meters, renewable-heavy grids, switchgear and energy-storage systems
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The centrepiece of expansion is a new manufacturing facility at Pune, Maharashtra, described as part of a forward-integration strategy and focused on the production of automotive busbars, connectors and their assemblies, with a focus on PCBA and busbar assembly solutions for high-growth areas such as e-mobility, energy storage and allied applications; the project carries a planned investment of approximately `200 million expected to be funded through internal accruals. The MD&A states the facility is operational and has commenced commercial production, processing orders and supplying against assembly commitments, and that it now works alongside the existing facilities at Solan, Himachal Pradesh, ensuring customer schedules continue to be met without interruption as the Pune operation scales towards full capacity; Pune is also described as an R&D and CCS project intended to shorten the loop between customer need, prototype, pilot lots and production scale-up through proximity to automotive and industrial ecosystems. Capacity headroom rather than greenfield build is the stated funding logic: the Company runs in-house stamping, tooling, R&D and reliability testing across three campuses in Solan and says the existing asset base can support more than `1,300 crore of revenue, so near-term growth carries low greenfield risk and high incremental returns, with forward integration, the Pune facility and capacity additions funded from internal accruals while maintaining a steady dividend. Alongside this, management is pursuing selective backward integration by processing some raw materials in-house to shorten the cash cycle, remains open to bolt-on acquisitions that add products or markets, and established Shivalik Bimetals Europe SRL in Milan, Italy as a wholly owned subsidiary to anchor the European recovery with direct access to EU customers. BRSR Section A records two national plants and one national office plus one international office, with a footnote that SBCL is setting up a new manufacturing facility/plant at Pune, Maharashtra.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Margin-led, value-led growth rather than volume-led: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 12.3% while EBITDA grew 26.0% and PAT 24.8%, with EBITDA margin up about 250 bps to 22.9% and gross margin up about 212 bps to 45.2%, driven by stronger realisations, improved product mix, operating leverage and disciplined cost governance
- Standalone revenue grew 5.7% to `462.0 crore despite volumes declining marginally by 0.6%, indicating improved average realisations
- Component-led supply share of 65%, up from around 55% in management commentary, with an indicative 10-12% improvement in realisation on component conversion
- Smart metering: management indicated revenue from smart meter applications nearly doubled during FY26, moving from a base of around `30-40 crore to more than `75-80 crore, linked also to localisation of relay and component manufacturing in India
- Shunt Resistors revenue grew 8.6% to `230.7 crore despite lower volumes, on improved customer mix, higher realisations and increased contribution from value-added components, with India up 27.4% on automotive, smart metering, current sensing, battery management and energy management demand and Europe up 14.5%
- Thermostatic Bimetals revenue grew 2.9% to `231.3 crore on improved realisations and export traction, with Europe up 47.0% to `50.7 crore, while domestic demand stayed moderate particularly in switchgear-linked applications
- Electrical Contacts grew strongly through the subsidiary platform, expanding by over 54%, supported by higher volumes and the pass-through of increased silver and other commodity prices
- Regional rebalancing: India remained the largest market at approximately `200.2 crore, Europe combined Shunt and Bimetal revenue grew 33.3% to `79.4 crore, Asia excluding India grew 24.2% to `79.9 crore, while the Americas declined 16.0% with early signs of demand normalisation as strip supplies convert into end products
- Structural electrification tailwind cited in MD&A: current measurement in EVs and smart meters, busbars and connections in battery and power-distribution systems, and switching and protection across an electrifying grid
- Automotive content-per-vehicle shift: the automotive software and electronics market is projected to grow about 4.5% annually to US$519 billion by 2035 against roughly 1% growth for the vehicle market, with power electronics among the fastest-growing hardware segments at nearly 10% a year
- India macro backdrop of durable consumption, a public capital expenditure cycle and lower policy rates underpinning demand across the Company's core electrical, automotive and industrial end-markets
- Trade backdrop is a two-sided driver: the headline trade tailwind is fading, but AI-enabling and advanced-manufacturing goods, electrification-linked inputs and a more multipolar customer base align with where higher-value demand is migrating
